description: Create a NEW version of the Generalist Gripper assembly used with SO-101 Arm 2 / Mount 2. Jake wants the finger/gripper working plane as clear as possible: his thumb/index finger and gripper fingers occupy that roughly 10–20mm vertical band (illustrative, measure actual geometry; not a fixed dimension). Relocate servo, drive gears and as much supporting hardware as feasible UP ABOVE the human hand/finger plane, separating the drivetrain plane from the gripper finger plane. Preserve geared actuation, useful opening/stroke, and real servo/horn/fastener interfaces. Use vertical shafts/posts or another justified transmission arrangement to reach the fingers, minimize obstructions in their plane, and check full motion plus screw/tool/cable access. This is a separate new SO-101-compatible version, not the concurrent HLS3606M small-servo task voice-d01680be. Identify correct newest compatible SO-101 base/gripper source, preserve Arm 2 / Mount 2 interface, bump only changed part counters, preserve existing versions. Publish live preview with side-view comparison highlighting occupied finger band and overhead drivetrain. Parameterize clearances; report CAD vs unverified physical ergonomics/strength. Coordinate with other HelpingHands worker before editing shared catalog or version registry. Use GPT-6.1 Sol medium.

results.identified_issue: Latest human steering on 2026-10-23 explicitly removes the handle interface and puts thumb/index outside the fingers. Base 20 deliberately forks compact Base 18 / Gripper 24, rather than continuing large wrist-compatible Base 19. Gripper 25 advances because root bore, root outline, retired outer hook protrusions and integral key change. Base counter advances for inverted drive, smaller pivots, bored journals/cap and new gear sockets. Arm/Mount do not change and no wrist mount is claimed; gallery flags Mount 2 pairing and hides Handle row. No other HelpingHands worker pane was active. Jake explicitly allocated this item CAD/catalog and voice-3f6ae8e1 hand overlay; README contains its mm/axes/pose contract without modifying that pebble. Two sector gears, purchased spline plate and actual HLS3606M retain their original size; rigid inversion plus 6.8 mm relative stack separation moves teeth entirely above band. Source dimensions in params.json; live Tune truly regenerates isolated geometry, verified at drive_gap=1.2 with unchanged bought-motor extents. 14 print/part meshes single-body watertight, genus tests pass. 121 poses x 91 pairs = 11011 overlap checks, no pair exclusions; screw probes omit intentional thread/spline engagement. Continuous X/Z extrema, positive wrong-phase and seating controls, lattice ligament 0.4047256 mm, distal blade surface fidelity all pass. Driver shafts tested over same poses: straight near-ear access fails (5.303831 mm3 motor overlap), 10 degree tilted 2.5x45 mm shafts pass, but PH0 engagement/tool handle clearance remains unverified and disclosed, rather than claiming physical assembly. 35 publisher/gallery/compact/legacy overhead tests pass. Broader pose suite has existing Base 6 v306 missing hinge entry; new row passes. No physical motor actuation, strength, ergonomics, resin fit, key/post bending, screw threads/pullout, cable bend or print support verification. Old design files untouched. Full metadata/exports with local .gitignore exception committed; app build not run.
results.summary: Created Base 20 and Gripper 25 with direct finger contact and a compact overhead drive.
results.detailed_description:
Removed the handles, strap-hook interface and long transmission shafts. Smaller 7 mm finger roots turn on 3 mm posts; short hex bosses connect directly to gears 0.8 mm above the 6 mm finger band. The inverted HLS3606M motor sits above them. Total Y stack is 53.2 mm.

Open Live Preview with Base 20 + Gripper 25, Arm/Mount off, and compare the attached top/side views. Full 0–30° sampled motion, mesh and gallery checks pass. This compact Base 18 derivative has no SO-101 wrist mount; the separate fit study owns the hand overlay.

Two motor-ear screws need a 10° tilted driver path: the shaft clears in CAD, but actual screw engagement is unverified. Hand comfort, printed strength and the assumed cable corridor also need physical checks; no motor was actuated.

results.notes: Latest Jake clarification overrides inherited handle-interface requirements for this NEW design: REMOVE the huge blue handles and their handle interface. User will manipulate the tweezer/gripper fingers DIRECTLY from their OUTSIDE faces, with thumb outside one finger and index outside the other; hand surrounds the grippers rather than occupying the inner grasping gap. Reconsider and shrink the rotary/pivot hub diameter now that the bulky handle interface is gone, subject to actual axle/bearing/gear/fastener wall thickness and stroke clearance. Do not retain large hubs solely for compatibility with removed handles. Keep latest minimal adjacent overhead drive plane and opposite-side motor placement. Preserve historic versions; bump changed parts only. Update preview hand fit and compatibility flags accordingly; no need to invent replacement straps/saddles unless direct contact requires a small justified contact surface. Coordinate with hand-fit item voice-3f6ae8e1. /Users/jakeschantz/HelpingHands

Jake feedback: drastically simplify the smaller gripper design. He likes moving drivetrain out of the finger Z plane, but the huge gap is unnecessary. Make a NEW version: motor remains ABOVE the fingers, but move it to the OPPOSITE SIDE of the current assembly and keep drive/mounting plane only JUST ABOVE the grippers, with minimum justified motion/fastener/cable clearance. It should sit at the EDGE of his hand: grippers in the thumb/index working band, motor/mounting immediately above that band, not a tall overhead tower. Revisit inverted motor/horn orientation and compact direct keyed/shaft coupling; delete long standoffs and unnecessary transfer structure wherever feasible. The 77.1mm derived lift in Base19 was not a requirement; do not preserve it by merely reducing overhead_gap. Compare side and top views before/after, document resulting gap and total height, and check full stroke + hardware assembly. Reference latest compact Base18/Gripper24 geometry as well as Base19 overhead design; Jake said smaller gripper, so explicitly identify chosen finger/servo source and favor compact geometry without silently claiming SO101 compatibility. Preserve existing versions. New part counters only for changed parts. Coordinate with thumb/index fit study voice-3f6ae8e1. Export/publish preview and validation. No physical motor actuation. Use GPT-6.1 Sol medium. /Users/jakeschantz/HelpingHands

results.identified_issue: Built on Base 15 / Gripper 22, newest full-size wrist-compatible source; Bases 16–18 are miniature incompatible alternatives, and HLS3606M task is already landed as Base 18. No other active HelpingHands worker pane was present; re-pulled and checked registry before adding Base 19. Base 19 alone advances. Original 12 mm finger slab, finger meshes, Mount 2 hub and tool plate retained exactly. Drivetrain translated +77.1 mm Y from derived servo/cable stack; 8 mm minimum cable corridor gap. Shaft sectors are integral, 16 mm journal, 12 mm finger shaft, hex lower web, separate washer with M3x12 retaining screw. Extended bracket preserves Mount 2 position. Full 121-pose / 153-pair sweep (18513 checks), horn tool probes, positive wrong-phase control and continuous vertex extrema pass. 14 print meshes watertight, single-body. 18 targeted publisher/mixed assembly tests pass. General pose suite fails only existing v306 missing pose entry. Added pinion hinge to Gripper 22 pose owner so the mixed Base 19 moves its drive; unchanged interface meshes compared at zero vertex error. Physical ergonomics, force, cantilever stiffness, printed-bearing wear, fastener fit/thread depth, real cable routing, slicer supports and whole-arm motion unverified. No app build performed.
results.summary: Created Base 19 with the STS3215 geared drive above the finger plane.
results.detailed_description:
Base 19 builds on full-size Base 15. The servo and gears sit above the measured 12 mm finger band; stepped shafts drive the original cradles below. Gripper 22, Arm 2 and Mount 2 stay unchanged. The reserved cable corridor clears the band by 8 mm.

Open Live Preview with Base 19 + Gripper 22 + Arm 2 + Mount 2. The side comparison shows the added overhead height. All 121 sampled motion poses and 18 publishing/assembly tests pass; the broader pose suite still flags an existing archived Base 6 entry.

This is CAD only: hand comfort, long-shaft stiffness, bearing wear and physical fastener/cable fit need testing before use.
